s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of severe upper abdominal pain with associated nausea and vomiting, worsened by oral intake, in a post-surgical patient
salient_findings: Sudden-onset, sharp upper abdominal pain rated 9/10
Pain worsened with oral intake
Associated nausea and vomiting
Generalized abdominal tenderness, most pronounced in the right hypochondrium
Cluster of small-bowel loops in the left upper quadrant on CT with spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels
key_facts: 36-year-old woman
Sudden-onset, sharp upper abdominal pain
Pain awakened her early in the morning
Pain rated 9/10
Pain minimally relieved by oxycodone
Pain worsened with oral intake
Associated nausea and vomiting
Unable to tolerate liquids or a soft diet
History of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass three weeks prior
History of intermittent nausea after surgery
Denies bloating, changes in bowel habits, or urinary symptoms
Medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus
Managed with pantoprazole, metformin, and semaglutide
History of laparoscopic cholecystectomy and other abdominal surgeries
Generalized abdominal tenderness on examination
Vital signs within normal limits
Laboratory studies showed normal hemoglobin, slightly elevated white-cell count, and normal liver function tests
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed cluster of small-bowel loops in the left upper quadrant with spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels

shortlist.label: Internal Hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Post-surgical patient with sudden-onset severe upper abdominal pain and CT findings of small-bowel loops with spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels

shortlist.label: Small Bowel Obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Severe abdominal pain worsened by oral intake and CT findings of clustered small-bowel loops

shortlist.label: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass Complication
shortlist.why_kept: Recent history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and presentation with severe upper abdominal pain and nausea

shortlist.label: Adhesional Band
shortlist.why_kept: History of multiple abdominal surgeries and presentation with severe abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Mesenteric Ischemia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe abdominal pain disproportionate to physical findings and CT findings of mesenteric vessel congestion

raw.rationale: The contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated a cluster of small-bowel loops in the left upper quadrant with a spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels, which is consistent with internal hernia, especially given the patient's recent history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery.

rejected.label: Small Bowel Obstruction
rejected.why: There were no signs of anastomotic leak, strangulation, or bowel obstruction on the CT scan.

rejected.label: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass Complication
rejected.why: While the patient had a recent Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, the specific findings on CT are more suggestive of internal hernia than a general complication of the surgery.

rejected.label: Adhesional Band
rejected.why: The CT findings and the patient's symptoms are more consistent with internal hernia than adhesional band, which might not cause such specific radiographic signs.

rejected.label: Mesenteric Ischemia
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory studies, including lactate levels, did not indicate mesenteric ischemia, and the CT findings were more suggestive of internal hernia.
